plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Before most trees have woken up, ume branches are covered in small, fragrant, five-petaled blossoms. They open on bare, dark twigs in shades of white, blush and deep rose. Their sweet, spicy scent drifts through gardens and orchards. It is one of East Asia's best-loved signs that winter is ending.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, roughly February through March
plants.location: Japan, where ume groves and shrine gardens are in flower in mid-March, and in temperate gardens across East Asia
plants.funFact: Ume often blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. Its fruit is pickled into umeboshi and steeped into plum wine.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Native British daffodils are smaller and daintier than garden hybrids. They have pale creamy-yellow outer petals around a deeper golden trumpet. In the damp woods, meadows and old pastures where they grow, they spread in drifts of nodding blooms. They bring light to the ground before the tree canopy leafs out.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, mainly March and April, and sometimes earlier in mild years
plants.location: Woodlands, meadows and pastures of the UK and western Europe, such as the Welsh borders and Gloucestershire
plants.funFact: Its common name, Lent lily, comes from its habit of flowering around the Christian season of Lent. It is the only daffodil native to Britain.
